Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 71
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: Oceania
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Painter
  trauma_type: Terrorism
  pcl5: 48

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Reassurance Seeking: I keep asking others to reassure me that I am okay, Emotion Control: I try hard to control my emotions, Avoid Going Out: Going out
  Memory: Bodily Reenactment: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred., Vivid Memory: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed., Uncontrolled Access: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
  Negative Appraisals: Can't Rely on Self: I can't rely on myself, Can't Rely on Others: I can't rely on other people, World is Dangerous: The world is a dangerous place

Vignette:
Seventy-one-year-old Thomas, of Oceania descent, has lived in America for over four decades. He worked as a painter until his recent traumatic experience left him reeling with fear and uncertainty. A few months ago, he was in the city center when a terrorist attack occurred, leaving chaos and destruction in its wake. The sudden explosions and gunfire that echoed through the streets sent Thomas into a state of shock. Despite escaping physical injury, the psychological toll has been immense. Since then, Thomas's life has become an intricate dance of seeking reassurance and trying to control his emotions. Each day, he finds himself reaching out to friends and neighbors, repeatedly asking if they think he will be alright or if the world is safe now. This constant need for validation stems from a deep-seated belief that he can't rely on himself, and even worse, that others are unreliable too. Thomas’s memories of the attack have been vivid and intrusive. When these memories surface, his body reenacts the positions it held during the event—his hands clench tightly as if to shield himself, and his heart races as if the danger is imminent once again. He recalls every detail—the sound of shattering glass, the smell of smoke, the sight of people running in panic—and these memories force their way into his mind at unexpected moments, disrupting his peace. His occupation has become a significant source of distress. Thomas used to enjoy painting murals around town, but now he finds it nearly impossible to leave his home without feeling overwhelmed by anxiety. The thought of being out in public triggers intense fear, making him avoid crowded places altogether. He’s canceled several jobs and his reputation as a reliable painter has suffered because of this. His clients have grown concerned about his availability, and some have even found other painters. The world feels dangerous to Thomas, and he is certain that it will never be safe again. This belief colors every aspect of his life. He avoids going out not just for work but also for simple pleasures like grocery shopping or visiting friends. His social interactions are limited, and he spends most days alone in his home, watching the news anxiously to see if there are any new threats. What frightens him most is the thought that another attack could happen at any moment. He feels vulnerable and helpless, and this sense of danger has seeped into every corner of his life. Despite these fears, he recognizes that avoiding everything will only make things worse in the long run. Thomas is beginning to understand that he needs professional help to navigate these overwhelming feelings. What brings him to therapy now is a deep hope for relief from the constant anxiety and fear. He hopes to regain some sense of control over his life, to be able to trust himself and others again, and to return to the work he once loved without being consumed by dread. Thomas wants to find a way back to living fully in the world, rather than hiding from it. The road ahead is uncertain for Thomas, but with therapy, he sees a chance at reclaiming his life, one step at a time. His fears are daunting, but so too is his desire for peace and stability.
